title: Sovereignty enforcement defaults to audit-only, and was unreachable from config
severity: Low if staged intentionally; Medium if believed-enforcing
finding: The evaluateSovereignty decision core is sound and fail-closed, but on the review-consumer path sovereigntyEnforce defaults to false — because modelClass is self-declared/spoofable until bound to a signing identity — so a sovereignty violation is logged (enforced: false) and not denied unless an operator turns enforcement on. Recommendation: state explicitly, in the deployment's security posture, whether production has sovereigntyEnforce on.

repros.verbatim: Exploit preconditions: production runs with sovereigntyEnforce off (the default) and an operator or the client believes the sovereignty guarantee is live. Repro status: not attempted — the default is confirmed in code.

captured_on.note: Backfilled after the fact (assay environment-attestation fix, prompted by Rob Chuvala/NWS: "what substrate were those captured on? If we didn't record it, we have cases locked against an unpinned baseline." — his question named the gap; this corpus originally answered it by capturing environment identity (OS/arch/kernel/bun/cortex-commit) under the wrong name, `SubstrateStamp` — see the ubiquitous-language fix that renamed it to `EnvironmentStamp` (lib/environment.ts) and added a genuine `substrate` field, meaning the coding harness (lib/substrate.ts), using the ecosystem's `HarnessId` vocabulary). This corpus's runner captured no environment stamp before the original fix, so the only thing honestly knowable is the date this case entered the corpus — from the corpus's own commit (2173581, 2026-07-27T11:57:28+12:00), NOT from provenance.date above (that's when the underlying finding was discovered, a different event). OS/arch/kernel/bun-version/cortex-commit were never recorded at capture time and are not reconstructable — do not infer them from the machine running this backfill, or from the cortex commit named in this case's `fix` field (that documents the FIX, not the verification environment). `substrate` (coding harness) is also left `null`: this case was in fact authored during a Claude Code session — commit 2173581 carries a `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5` trailer, and the later environment-attestation commit 94e6598 carries a `Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_...` trailer, both consistent with Claude Code — but neither is a captured substrate stamp, so this is recollection backed by circumstantial commit evidence, not a record. Left `null` rather than asserted `claude-code`, per this corpus's own no-guessing rule.

expected: policy.sovereignty.enforce must be a real, documented, principal-settable config key (not merely a constructor-only test hook unreachable from any config file), threaded identically to both consumers that evaluate sovereignty, defaulting to false with the posture honestly logged at boot as audit-only, not enforcing.

fix.summary: EBH-6b: added policy.sovereignty.enforce (boolean, default false), resolved once in cortex.ts and threaded to both review-consumer.ts and brain-consumer.ts. The EBH-6 investigation (docs/security/ebh-6-posture-findings.md) additionally found the gap was WORSE than reported: sovereigntyEnforce wasn't just defaulted off, it was constructor-only — no config field could reach it at all before this fix, in either consumer.

verification.note: Greps src/cortex.ts for the single resolved `sovereigntyEnforce` value and confirms it is passed to BOTH consumer construction sites — the exact asymmetry the EBH-6 investigation found and closed. Does not spin up a live bus/consumer; that would need a running stack.

notes: Enforcement is STILL off by default in every shipped template — this fix makes the posture honest and reachable, it does not flip enforcement on. Do not read 'fixed' here as 'sovereignty is now enforced by default' — it is not, and per the hardening plan should not be until model-class-to-signing-identity binding (cortex#2117) lands.
